Whole + Gemini.summary:
Ren Suzuki is a 1-year-old girl with no documented past medical history, medications, or allergies who presented on 04/01/2026 with approximately 24 hours of right ear pain, irritability, frequent crying, reduced feeding, sleep difficulty, and right ear pulling. She was afebrile and clinically stable, with mild right outer-ear erythema and tenderness. Otoscopy showed a bulging, mildly erythematous right tympanic membrane with effusion; the left ear was normal. There was no otorrhoea, mastoiditis, cellulitis, neurological deficit, or systemic infection.

She was diagnosed with acute right otitis media with effusion and admitted under Paediatrics/ENT for management. Oral paracetamol 120 mg was administered for pain, and oral amoxicillin was commenced at 125 mg/5 mL three times daily for 5 days. Paracetamol was continued four times daily or as needed, with warm compresses advised. Parents received education regarding ear care, medication administration, completion of antibiotics, expected improvement, and red-flag symptoms. Pharmacy review confirmed the amoxicillin regimen as appropriate, with no changes.

On review the following morning, she had significant improvement in pain, was alert and comfortable, and had tolerated oral antibiotics and analgesia without adverse effects. Right tympanic membrane erythema and effusion had decreased, with no systemic infection or distress. She was planned for discharge later that day with amoxicillin 125 mg/5 mL, 2.5 mL three times daily for 5 days, and paracetamol 120 mg/5 mL, 5 mL four times daily as needed for pain. ENT follow-up was advised in 2 weeks, and the GP was informed of the discharge plan on 05/01/2026.
